summary: In browser-use, the AI model chooses the actions on each of its steps (code may first open a web address named in the task) and decides the task is finished by calling done. Among the decisions this map shows, nobody is asked before an action runs, so a form submit or a script the model writes goes ahead on its own, and code clicks OK on alerts and confirm dialogs. The built-in limits on how long a run goes are counts, not judgments (500 steps, or 5 failed steps in a row), and the run's success flag is the model's value when it gives one and true when it does not; a second model call grades the run without changing that flag.

judgments.question: Before the agent submits, buys, sends, deletes or runs page JavaScript, does anyone approve it?
judgments.answer: Nobody is asked: the model's actions run as soon as they are parsed. An integrator can add a check in their own code through the step callback, which sees the proposed actions before they run.

judgments.question: Which actions is the model offered this step?
judgments.answer: Every built-in action on every page, including evaluate, which runs JavaScript the model writes, except screenshot at the default vision setting and any the integrator excluded, plus custom actions whose site filter matches. On the last step or after repeated failures, only done.

judgments.question: When a page opens a JavaScript dialog, who decides OK or Cancel?
judgments.answer: Code clicks OK on every alert, confirm and leave-page dialog the moment it opens, and Cancel on every text prompt, before the model sees it; the model is told afterwards.

judgments.question: Which browser permissions are granted to the sites the agent visits?
judgments.answer: When the browser connects, code grants clipboard read/write and notifications to every site; any other permission a page asks for is left to Chrome.

judgments.question: When a page offers a file, is it saved to disk?
judgments.answer: Yes. Downloads are always allowed, into a fresh temporary folder, and by default PDFs and attachments are also saved without a click.

judgments.question: Is the task finished?
judgments.answer: The model decides by calling done; code ends the run on that call without checking whether the answer is right, and the judge only grades it afterwards.

judgments.question: Did the task succeed, by the agent's own report?
judgments.answer: The success flag is whatever the model puts in done. If the model leaves it out, code records success, and with an output schema the field is hidden from the model.

judgments.question: Does an independent judge think the task succeeded?
judgments.answer: On by default: after a done, a second call through the agent's own model client grades the run against the task and the last 10 screenshots. The verdict is logged; the agent's own success flag stands.

judgments.question: When has the run used up its step budget?
judgments.answer: After 500 steps by default; code records "Failed to complete task in maximum steps" and returns with no answer.

judgments.question: When does the agent give up after repeated failures?
judgments.answer: After 5 failed steps in a row (the default), the model gets one step that may only call done; if that fails too, the run ends.

judgments.question: While the agent runs, may a person at the terminal halt it, and how does it resume?
judgments.answer: On Mac and Linux, Ctrl+C pauses the run and a second press quits; on Windows the first press quits. Pressing Enter does not resume, despite the printed hint: only code calling agent.resume() does.

judgments.question: What should the agent do next?
judgments.answer: Every step, the model (by default Browser Use's hosted bu-2-0) reads the task, the page and the history and returns up to five actions; code runs them in order.

problems.title: A run can be reported successful when the model never said so
problems.plain: A program reads the success flag in the model's done call at the end of a run. If the model leaves the flag out, code records success. When the developer asks for a structured result, that field is hidden from the model, so such a run normally reads as successful unless the model sets it anyway. An open pull request in browser-use's tracker proposes a fix.

problems.title: After a step times out, the model is not told which of its actions already ran
problems.plain: A whole step gets 180 seconds by default. If it runs over, it is cut off, the record of which of the step's actions finished is dropped, and the step's result is only a timeout error. If the run takes another step, the model sees the page as it now is, which may show some effects, but it is not told which of its actions already ran. We found no report of this in browser-use's tracker.

problems.title: Pressing Enter does not resume a paused run, though the message says it will
problems.plain: On Mac and Linux, pressing Ctrl+C pauses the run and prints "Press [Enter] to resume or [Ctrl+C] again to quit". Pressing Enter does not resume it; only code that calls agent.resume() does, so a person at the terminal can quit with a second Ctrl+C but cannot continue the run from there. We found no report of this in browser-use's tracker.
